en.headline: Government begins first phase of Bishop Hill clearance
en.dek: Authorities started removing unauthorised structures and facilities on the Sham Shui Po hillside today, sealing one side for about three days while keeping access open via the other entrance.
body: The Home Affairs Department said the first phase of clearance work on Bishop Hill, also known as Wo Tsai Shan, began on Wednesday. The operation targets illegal and unsafe structures, facilities and debris on government land.

The Lands Department had posted statutory notices on 10 August requiring owners of the affected objects to stop occupying the land by 12 August. Workers and uniformed police were present as items including fitness equipment and table-tennis tables were removed from the sealed section running from the Tong Yin Street side to the summit.

Each phase is expected to take about three days of partial closure. During the works the public can still use the opposite entrance near Berwick Street to reach the former Sham Shui Po service reservoir and other open areas. Religious items on the hill are being handled with the assistance of religious leaders, the department said.

After clearance is complete, the government plans to install new recreational facilities, reinforce slopes and make other improvements under an optimisation scheme. The second phase will cover the Berwick Street side of the hill.

zh.headline: 政府展開主教山首階段清場
zh.dek: 當局今日開始清理深水埗窩仔山違法及不安全構築物，首階段圍封棠蔭街一邊約三日，另一邊入口仍可供市民上山。
body: 民政事務總署表示，窩仔山（俗稱主教山）優化計劃首階段清理工作於周三展開，目標是移除官地上違法及不安全的構築物、設施及雜物。
地政總署已於8月10日就首階段範圍張貼法定通知，要求相關人士於8月12日前停止佔用土地。今日有地政職員、軍裝警及搬運工人到場，搬走健身器材及乒乓球枱等物品，範圍由棠蔭街山邊休憩處至山頂。
署方指每階段會圍封山邊一邊約三日以確保安全，其間市民仍可使用近巴域街的另一邊入口上山，包括前往山頂前深水埗配水庫。山上宗教物品已邀請宗教領袖協助妥善處理。
清理完成後，政府會解封現場，並在合適安全地點建設新的康體及休憩設施、加固斜坡等優化項目。次階段將處理近巴域街山腳至山頂範圍。
